rationale: Permit a weak region to contain up to two cells of the same four-medoid partition, keeping the auxiliary embedding and predictive model fixed. Across seeds, selected single cells have similar contrasts (0.0573–0.0616) and shares (11.56%–12.43%), but different profiles: business_receipt_share has median 0.709 in run:73103 versus approximately 0.274 in the other runs, while documentation_gap_z is 0.847 versus approximately 1.46. Together with much higher contrasts in small frontier cells, this motivates testing whether distinct error-associated profiles can jointly form a supported region without the dilution required by one nearest-medoid cell. Medoid replacement can move cell boundaries but cannot directly express a union. This is a hypothesis about representational capacity, not evidence that numerical optimization reached a global optimum.
falsifiable_prediction: Under the same region-score budget, support rules and >=10% reporting threshold, the union-enabled search will find a two-cell region with greater Brier contrast than equal-budget single-cell continuation. The selected improvement should persist on independent confirmation under the prescribed measurement procedure; failure to improve would count against the proposed representation limitation.
alternative_explanations: Seed differences and late frontier improvements may reflect remaining numerical search opportunity within the current representation.
Different region medians may describe overlapping populations rather than complementary error-associated groups.
The contrast–share tradeoff may reflect genuine concentration of errors in small populations, so adding another cell could dilute contrast.
Adaptive reuse of the discovery sample may explain apparent gains.
limitations: The packet does not provide losses for every cell within each partition or membership overlaps, so it does not establish that a beneficial pair exists.
Cells from different runs cannot simply be combined; both cells must belong to one candidate partition.
A fixed auxiliary embedding may itself omit useful error structure, which unions cannot recover.
All existing support and measurement rules remain applicable. No causal interpretation or confirmed weakness is asserted; the numerical evaluator determines benefit.
